qa.name: Abductor Pollicis Brevis
qa.origin: Flexor retinaculum, tubercle of the scaphoid, and tubercle of the trapezium
qa.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
qa.innervation: Recurrent branch of the median nerve
qa.function: Abduction of the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint
qa.blood_supply: Superficial palmar branch of the radial artery
qa.clinical_note: First muscle to show wasting in carpal tunnel syndrome — innervated by the recurrent branch of the median nerve which loops around the distal edge of the flexor retinaculum

qa.name: Flexor Pollicis Brevis
qa.origin: Superficial head — flexor retinaculum and trapezium; Deep head — trapezoid and capitate
qa.insertion: Base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
qa.innervation: Superficial head — recurrent branch of the median nerve; Deep head — deep branch of the ulnar nerve
qa.function: Flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint of the thumb
qa.blood_supply: Superficial palmar branch of the radial artery
qa.clinical_note: Has a dual nerve supply — the only thenar muscle with both median and ulnar innervation; the deep head is spared in carpal tunnel syndrome

qa.name: Opponens Pollicis
qa.origin: Flexor retinaculum and tubercle of the trapezium
qa.insertion: Lateral surface of the first metacarpal along its entire length
qa.innervation: Recurrent branch of the median nerve
qa.function: Opposition of the thumb — medial rotation and flexion of the first metacarpal
qa.blood_supply: Superficial palmar branch of the radial artery
qa.clinical_note: Produces the uniquely human movement of opposition — loss of opposition from median nerve injury severely impairs pinch and grip; tested by touching thumb to little finger

qa.name: Adductor Pollicis
qa.origin: Oblique head — bases of second and third metacarpals, capitate, and adjacent carpals; Transverse head — anterior surface of the third metacarpal
qa.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
qa.innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
qa.function: Adduction of the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint, assists in pinch grip
qa.opposing_muscle: Abductor Pollicis Brevis, Abductor Pollicis Longus
qa.clinical_note: Innervated by the ulnar nerve — not the median nerve; Froment sign tests adductor pollicis weakness by asking the patient to hold paper between thumb and index finger
